newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Dolenjska says Daiwa after stake in bank.
newsitem.headline: Dolenjska says Daiwa after stake in bank.

text.p: Slovenian bank Dolenjska banka said on Monday it planned to open itself to foreign shareholders and that Japan's Daiwa Bank had cited interest in taking a stake.
"The shareholders will decide whether to enable a 15-percent foreign ownership in the bank at the meeting on May 20," deputy chief executive Milena Dular told Reuters.
Daiwa had voiced interest in buying into the tiny Alpine republic's eighth largest bank but the purchase would first need approval from the Bank of Slovenia, she said.
The bank's ordinary shares jumped 3.33 percent to 15,500 tolars and the preferred shares closed 3.57 percent higher at 14,500 tolars on the news.
"The rise is the result of the news that Daiwa is seriously interested in Dolenjska banka and also of Dolenjska's good business results announced recently," one trader said.
The share price could surge as high as 20,000 tolars in the next two weeks, he added.

In April, the bank reported 1996 net profit rose to 478 million tolars from 400 million and added it planned to pay an unchanged dividend of 800 tolars per share. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 156.7 Slovenian Tolars)
